input.question: Would a suction cup still have the ability to stick to a surface in a vacuum?
input.ground_truth: When a suction cup is pressed against a surface, it pushes out all of the air beneath it and creates a vacuum between the cup and the surface. This vacuum holds the suction cup tightly, and it will continue to do so until the pressure on the outside of the cup becomes lower than the pressure on the inside of the cup. (from [ehow](_URL_0_)) In a vacuum, the pressure outside will be the same as the pressure outside, so no, it will not stick to a surface.

Okay! Imagine you have a suction cup, like the kind you see on a toy that sticks to the wall.

Now, let’s think about what helps the suction cup stick. It’s like when you put a cup over something and push it down. The air tries to get out, but can’t, so it makes a “suck” feeling that holds the cup on the wall.

But in a vacuum, there is no air at all! There’s nothing for the suction cup to “suck” because there’s no air to push or pull.

So, the suction cup won’t stick to the wall in a vacuum, because it needs air to make that “suck” work.

It’s like trying to blow up a balloon with no air around—it just won’t work!
